draft.title: Faraday's laws
card: The amount of substance made in electrolysis depends on the charge passed through the cell. More charge means more product.
Charge in coulombs is current in amperes multiplied by time in seconds. Q = It. Convert minutes and hours to seconds first.
The amount of electrons in moles is n(e⁻) = Q/F. F is Faraday's constant, about 96 500 C mol⁻¹. It is the charge carried by one mole of electrons.
Use the half-equation to link electrons to product. For Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu, two moles of electrons make one mole of copper.
draft.remember: Q = It, then n(e⁻) = Q/F, then use the half-equation ratio.

a.q: A current of 2.0 A flows for 100 s in an electrolytic cell. What charge passes through the cell?
a.why: Q = It = 2.0 × 100 = 200 C. Dividing current by time gives 0.020, which is the wrong operation. 96 500 C is the charge of one mole of electrons, not this cell.
a.clue: Multiply current by time in seconds.

b.q: A current of 1.93 A flows for 5000 s through molten silver nitrate. Ag⁺ + e⁻ → Ag. How many moles of silver form at the cathode?
b.why: Q = 1.93 × 5000 = 9650 C. n(e⁻) = 9650 ÷ 96 500 = 0.100 mol. One electron makes one silver atom, so n(Ag) = 0.100 mol. 0.0500 mol would come from wrongly halving the electrons.
b.clue: Find Q, then electrons, then use the 1 to 1 ratio.

check.summary: No problems found. Both calculations are correct (200 C; 9650 C gives 0.100 mol e⁻ and 0.100 mol Ag), and the card matches the VCE data book value of F.
